universities.name: RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences
universities.summary: RCSI University of Medicine and Health Sciences has trained doctors since 1784 and is Ireland's largest medical school. Its Direct Entry Medicine programme leads to the National University of Ireland MB, BCh, BAO degree, accredited by the Irish Medical Council, with the underlying Irish medical qualification carrying EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU/EEA since Ireland's 1976 accession to the mechanism.
universities.campusLifestyle: RCSI's Direct Entry Medicine programme offers 75 EU and 225 non-EU places per year, taught through Case-Based Learning in small groups of around 12 students, with a Personal Tutor assigned to every student and six cross-year learning communities. RCSI states it is among the first Irish higher-education institutions authorised by Quality and Qualifications Ireland to use the TrustEd Ireland mark.
universities.cityProfile: Dublin is Ireland's capital, and RCSI's central-Dublin campus sits close to its own Mercer Court student residence, a short walk from the city centre. RCSI is recognised by the US Department of Education's Federal Student Aid programme as an eligible foreign institution (school code 00770500) for its Medicine, Physiotherapy and Pharmacy programmes.
universities.practicalExposure: The Direct Entry Medicine programme runs across three stages -- Foundation of Practice (Years 1-2), Integration into Practice (Year 3), and Preparation for Practice (Years 4-5) -- with a preceding Foundation Year for the 6-year track. Clinical placements from Year 3 run across RCSI's teaching hospitals, including Beaumont Hospital, Connolly Hospital, the Rotunda Hospital, Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital Drogheda, Cavan and Monaghan Hospital, and Louth County Hospital, alongside a wider affiliated network including the National Maternity Hospital and Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin. Year 4 places students full-time on hospital clinical teams across Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Psychiatry, Surgery, Paediatrics and General Practice, and Year 5 concludes with a sub-internship clerkship. Graduates who complete Ireland's 12-month intern year and receive a Certificate of Experience are exempt from the Irish Medical Council's PRES pre-registration exam before full registration.
universities.hostelOverview: RCSI operates its own Mercer Court residence (Millin House plus Mercer Apartments), a short walk from campus, with 24/7 security and a dedicated accommodation manager. For a 41-week lease (11 September 2026-25 June 2027), Mercer Apartments run EUR 322/week single (EUR 13,202 total) or EUR 220/week twin (EUR 9,020 total), and Millin House runs EUR 332/week single (EUR 13,612 total) or EUR 244/week twin (EUR 10,004 total). Students who prefer private rental can use RCSI Student Services' guidance, though the university does not book private housing on students' behalf.
universities.dietarySupport: No specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure is published. Mercer Court residences include shared or communal kitchens; food costs should be planned as part of an independent living-cost budget.
universities.safetyOverview: No university-published campus-safety statistics were found. Mercer Court residence includes 24/7 security and a dedicated accommodation manager for resident students.
universities.studentSupport: Every student is assigned a Personal Tutor, and the curriculum is built around six cross-year learning communities with a positive-education-informed, well-being-focused design. RCSI Student Services provides accommodation guidance, and international scholarship queries go through the RCSI Admissions Office.
whyChoose: A medical school with a continuous history since 1784, Ireland's largest, whose Irish medical qualification carries EU Directive 2005/36/EC automatic recognition across the EU/EEA once the Irish intern year and Certificate of Experience are completed.
Recognised as an eligible foreign institution by the US Department of Education's Federal Student Aid programme for its Medicine programme (school code 00770500).
A detailed, country-specific entry-requirements framework covering A Levels, IB, US, Indian, Canadian, Australian, Gulf and other qualification systems for non-EU applicants.
A dedicated non-EU merit scholarship (International Consilio Manuque Medicine Scholarship, EUR 25,000 total, disbursed across the programme) with a transparent application and interview process.

Clinical training across a large, named network of RCSI teaching and affiliated hospitals, including Ireland's national referral centres for neurosurgery and renal transplantation at Beaumont Hospital.

faq.question: Is the Direct Entry Medicine programme different from Graduate Entry Medicine?
faq.answer: Yes. Direct Entry Medicine (DEM) admits students straight from secondary education; Graduate Entry Medicine (GEM) is a separate 4-year programme for applicants who already hold a bachelor's degree. This record covers Direct Entry Medicine only.

faq.question: What qualification is awarded on graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates receive the MB, BCh, BAO (Hons), a National University of Ireland degree at Level 8 on Ireland's National Framework of Qualifications, accredited by the Irish Medical Council.

faq.question: How long is the programme?
faq.answer: 5 years for applicants exempt from the Foundation Year, or 6 years (including a Foundation Year) for others, based on the applicant's prior secondary-school qualifications as assessed by the Admissions Committee.

faq.question: What is the current tuition fee?
faq.answer: EUR 61,000 per year for non-EU students, plus a once-off EUR 135 National University of Ireland registration fee (EUR 61,135 total in year one). Non-EU fees have historically risen by roughly 2% a year.

faq.question: What entrance route does the university use for non-EU applicants?
faq.answer: Non-EU applicants do not sit HPAT-Ireland (that applies only to the Irish/EU school-leaver route). Instead, RCSI assesses non-EU applicants against published country-specific academic criteria, such as A Level AAB including Chemistry, or IB 38+ with Chemistry at Higher Level.

faq.question: When does the academic year start, and when can I apply?
faq.answer: The single annual intake starts in September. The September 2026 intake has already closed. For September 2027 entry, non-EU applications (excluding USA/Canada) open 1 November 2026 and close 15 January 2027; USA/Canada applicants apply via Atlantic Bridge, opening 1 August 2026.

faq.question: Is a scholarship available for non-EU Medicine students?
faq.answer: Yes -- the International Consilio Manuque Medicine Scholarship offers EUR 25,000 total, disbursed across the programme (EUR 5,000/year on the 5-year track, EUR 4,167/year on the 6-year track), open to self-funding non-EU students admitted to the programme who have accepted their offer.

faq.question: Is university accommodation available for international students?
faq.answer: Yes -- RCSI's own Mercer Court residence offers single and twin rooms a short walk from campus, priced per a 41-week lease. Students can contact accommodation@rcsi.ie to apply, or use RCSI Student Services' guidance for private rental.

faq.question: Do Indian students need NEET to join this programme?
faq.answer: RCSI's own admissions criteria do not reference NEET, though the university advises Indian applicants to separately check India's National Medical Commission requirements. NEET-UG is required for Indian citizens and OCI holders pursuing a primary medical qualification abroad, as the mandatory Eligibility Certificate.

ctas.label: Build my cost and funding plan

fee.notes: Officially published non-EU tuition: EUR 61,000/year, plus a once-off EUR 135 National University of Ireland registration fee (EUR 61,135 total in year one), per RCSI's official Fees and Funding page. Non-EU fees have historically risen roughly 2%/year; the 6-year total is a calculated estimate (61,000 x 6 + 135) assuming no increase and is not an official locked-in figure. A EUR 75 application fee applies separately. Refund policy: 50% of annual tuition due by 1 July, a 14-day cooling-off period follows, withdrawal after 31 January makes the student liable for 100% of that year's tuition, and visa refusal triggers a full refund.

eligibleAudiences: International (non-EU) applicants meeting RCSI's country-specific academic criteria (e.g. A Level AAB including Chemistry, IB 38+ with Chemistry HL 5, or equivalent), with English proficiency at IELTS 6.5 overall (no band below 6.0) or exemption
restrictions: Applicants must have turned 18 by 31 December following entry
Programme length (5 or 6 years) is assigned by the Admissions Committee based on prior qualifications, not chosen by the applicant
Indian applicants must separately hold a current NEET-UG qualification under India's National Medical Commission rules; this is not administered by the university itself
audienceEligibility.notes: Non-EU applicants do not sit HPAT-Ireland (required only for the Irish/EU school-leaver route). USA/Canada-resident applicants apply via RCSI's partner, Atlantic Bridge, rather than directly.

admissionsContent.overview: Non-EU applicants (outside USA/Canada) apply directly via RCSI's website within the published window, pay the application fee, and submit academic and supporting documents; USA/Canada-resident applicants apply through RCSI's partner, Atlantic Bridge, on a separate timeline.

eligibility.intro: Admission requires meeting RCSI's country-specific academic threshold (e.g. A Levels, IB, or national equivalents with required Chemistry and science grades), English proficiency, and being at least 18 by 31 December following entry.
items: Country-specific academic threshold, e.g. A Level AAB including Chemistry (UK), IB 38+ with Chemistry HL 5 (International Baccalaureate), or 90% overall with 75%+ in Chemistry, Biology and Physics/Maths (India)
English proficiency: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (certificate under 2 years old), or exemption for wholly English-medium qualifications such as A Levels or IB
Minimum age: 18 by 31 December following entry
Indian applicants: current NEET-UG qualification per India's National Medical Commission rules, separate from the university's own admission process

applicationSteps: Apply directly via RCSI's website within the published application window (or via Atlantic Bridge if resident in the USA/Canada)
Pay the non-refundable EUR 75 application fee
Submit certified academic transcripts, a passport copy, a passport-style photo and a personal statement
Provide confidential referee contact details; RCSI contacts the referee directly for a reference
Submit supplementary documents evidencing relevant life experience (work, extracurriculars, volunteering) where applicable

academic: Certified academic transcripts (plus English-language transcripts or IELTS certificate where applicable)
Evidence meeting the applicant's country-specific academic threshold for Direct Entry Medicine
application: Passport copy (name, nationality and date-of-birth page)

visaConsiderations: RCSI's own refund policy guarantees a full fee refund if a student cannot obtain the required visa; confirm current Irish student-visa requirements directly with RCSI or Irish immigration authorities.

teachingPhases.details: An optional Foundation Year covers biomedical sciences and professionalism ahead of Years 1-2, which build anatomical, molecular, biochemical and pharmacological foundations through Case-Based Learning in small groups.
Hospital-based clinical placements begin at RCSI-affiliated teaching hospitals, alongside a simulation module and a Student Selected research or audit project.
Full-time clinical team placements across Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Psychiatry, Surgery, Paediatrics and General Practice, concluding with a mandatory sub-internship clerkship.
